description: Curated SPHEREx demo fields for Hiraya. Coordinates are ICRS degrees. Pull with: python tools/pull_targets.py

targets.name: Barnard's Star
targets.why: Fastest known stellar proper motion (~10″/yr) — stars drift visibly across SPHEREx revisits.

targets.name: Epsilon Indi Ba/Bb
targets.why: Nearby T-dwarf binary around ε Ind — cool objects that light up in SPHEREx mid-IR bands.

targets.name: WISE 0855−0714
targets.why: Coldest known brown dwarf; high proper motion (~8″/yr). User-supplied position.

targets.name: RW Aurigae
targets.why: Classical T Tauri binary with dramatic IR brightness swings and jets.

targets.name: R Draconis
targets.why: Mira-type AGB variable — strong mid-IR dust emission, large amplitude.

targets.name: Kapteyn's Star
targets.why: Halo subdwarf with huge proper motion — clean motion demo in the south.

targets.name: Luhman 16 AB
targets.why: Nearest brown-dwarf binary (~6.5 ly); bright in SPHEREx bands, high PM.

targets.name: Mira (ο Ceti)
targets.why: Prototype Mira variable + companion; classic IR light-curve / spectrum target.

targets.name: χ Cygni
targets.why: Extremely large-amplitude Mira; often among the brightest AGB stars in the mid-IR.

targets.name: Comet 3I/ATLAS
targets.why: IRSA published dedicated SPHEREx spectral images of interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS — great moving-object demo.
targets.notes: Approximate field; refine with IRSA MOST / Horizons before science use. See https://irsa.ipac.caltech.edu/data/SPHEREx/docs/comet3iatlas/index.html

targets.name: Pluto
targets.why: Slow solar-system mover across multi-visit stacks — good tracklet / blink demo.
targets.notes: Approximate 2025–2026 field; update ephemeris for exact epoch matching.
